formation.title: The Cross Upon the Shore
formation.text:
The ancient ports of North Africa (Carthage, Tunis, Tripoli) are ours. Where once the armies of Louis the Saint perished in the sands, where the knights of the Barbary Crusade raised their banners before Mahdia, a Christian kingdom now stands on African soil. The Mediterranean is no longer a frontier but a lake, its southern shore secured by the Cross. Yet the question of what this kingdom shall become weighs upon us. Our military orders possess hardened garrisons and mighty fortresses, while the merchant republics of Italy eye our ports with undisguised avarice. Shall we be the sword arm of Christendom in Africa, an unbreakable bulwark against the infidel? Or shall we be the bridge between continents, a trading emporium where the wealth of Africa, Europe, and the Orient mingles in our bazaars?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Deus vult! Our fortresses shall never fall!

modifiers.name: Sword of the Cross
modifiers.text: The banner of Christ flies over Africa. Our crusader knights are the hardened veterans of a holy war, fighting with the fervor of men who believe God marches at their side. The fortresses we build shall be the bulwarks of Christendom on a hostile shore.

effects.name: War Score vs other Religion Efficiency

options.text: Commerce enriches where conquest merely destroys.

modifiers.name: African Emporium
modifiers.text: The ports of Tunis and Tripoli command the narrows of the Mediterranean. Under Christian stewardship, these ancient trading cities flourish once more. Genoese, Venetian, and Catalan merchants fill our fondaci with goods from three continents, and the wealth of Africa flows through our customs houses.

advances.name: Ribats of the Orders
advances.text: The ribats of the Ifriqiyan coast, fortress houses raised by the Aghlabid emirs for warriors under vows, are handed to the brother knights of the crusade. Their walls are kept, their prayer halls are consecrated as chapels, and new houses are built inland on the same plan.

advances.name: Outremer Sergeants
advances.text: The tradition of heavy infantry sergeants-at-arms who form the backbone of crusader field armies and garrison forces.

advances.name: Crusader Zeal
advances.text: The religious fervor that drives the crusader state, making wars against heathens both cheaper and more popular among the faithful.

advances.name: Pilgrim Routes
advances.text: The establishment of pilgrim hospices and way stations along the routes to the holy sites of North Africa, including the ruins of ancient Carthage.

advances.name: Order Discipline
advances.text: The strict monastic discipline of the military orders, where daily prayer and drill produce soldiers of exceptional steadfastness.

advances.name: Turcopole Tradition
advances.text: The practice of recruiting local converts and mixed-heritage horsemen as light cavalry, continuing the tradition first established in the Levantine crusader states.

advances.name: The Royal Dogana
advances.text: The customs house the Hafsid emirs kept at Tunis, the diwan that the Italians called dogana, is taken over by the crown and copied in every port. All goods landed by foreign merchants pass through it, are taxed there, and are sold under its guarantee.

advances.name: Cathedral Chapters
advances.text: Cathedrals rise over the ruins of the Roman basilicas at Carthage and Hippo, where Augustine once preached. Their chapters anoint the kingdom's rulers and keep its charters.

advances.name: Charters of Settlement
advances.text: Settlers from Sicily, Provence and Catalonia are drawn across the sea by charters of franchise: a house plot and fields held for a fixed rent, and a court of their own burgesses. New villages rise around the old towns of Ifriqiya.

advances.name: African Coral Trade
advances.text: The harvesting and export of precious Mediterranean red coral from the waters off the Barbary Coast, a luxury good in demand across Europe and the East.

advances.name: Presidio System
advances.text: A network of fortified coastal strongpoints garrisoned by professional soldiers, controlling the harbors and approaches to the kingdom's cities.

event.title: The Presidio Network
event.text: The coastal fortifications of Crusader Africa have matured from crude stockades into a formidable system of star forts and walled presidios. From La Goletta guarding the approaches to Tunis, to the bastions of Tripoli overlooking the harbor, each fortress commands its stretch of coastline with interlocking fields of fire. Garrison commanders drill their musketeers daily, and the walls are thick enough to withstand bombardment from the heaviest Ottoman siege guns. Local converts serve alongside European soldiers, bound by shared faith and the knowledge that surrender means death or slavery. This presidio network is the backbone of Christian Africa, as long as these walls stand, the kingdom endures.

options.text: Let them break upon our walls like waves upon the shore.

modifiers.name: Bulwark of the Faith
modifiers.text: A network of fortified presidios guards every approach to our African dominions. Behind their walls, Christian settlers live in security, and no raiding party passes unchallenged.

options.text: Turn our fortresses into trading posts.

modifiers.name: Presidio Trade
modifiers.text: The coastal presidios serve a dual purpose, their walls protect not only soldiers but merchants, and their harbors become thriving trade centers where African and European goods change hands.

advances.name: Corsair Fleet
advances.text: A fleet of fast, oar-driven galleys operating from the ports of Tunis and Tripoli, patrolling the narrows of the Mediterranean and raiding hostile shipping.

advances.name: Mediterranean Trade Dominance
advances.text: Control of the central Mediterranean narrows gives Crusader Africa leverage over the trade between the eastern and western basins of the sea.

advances.name: Olive Oil Export
advances.text: The fertile lands of Ifriqiya produce abundant olive harvests, and the kingdom's oil presses supply lamp oil and cooking fat to markets across the Mediterranean.

advances.name: The Crusade Tithe
advances.text: As the last active crusader state, Crusader Africa is granted the crusade tithe, a share of church revenues from across Catholic Europe, and the legates of Rome plead its cause at every court.

advances.name: Local Militia
advances.text: The organization of local converts and second-generation settlers into militia companies for garrison duty and territorial defense.

advances.name: Confessional State
advances.text: The kingdom doubles down on its Catholic identity in the age of Reformation, positioning itself as a bastion of orthodoxy amid the religious upheaval of Europe.

advances.name: Trans-Mediterranean Commerce
advances.text: The kingdom's ports serve as transshipment points for goods moving between the Atlantic economies and the Levantine trade, profiting from every exchange.

advances.name: Assizes of the High Court
advances.text: The customs of the kingdom's High Court, where the king sits with his barons after the manner of the old court of Jerusalem, are set down in a written book of assizes. Pleas are heard by the book, and the officers of the crown are named and sworn before the court.

advances.name: Star Fortification
advances.text: Italian military engineers redesign the kingdom's defenses along modern principles, replacing medieval walls with angled bastions that deflect cannonballs.

advances.name: Order Marines
advances.text: An elite corps of amphibious soldiers trained in naval assault, coastal raids, and fortress storming operations.

event.title: Marines of the Order
event.text: The military orders of Crusader Africa have long recognized that their kingdom's survival depends on command of the sea. A new corps of Order Marines has been raised, elite soldiers trained to fight from ship to shore, scaling fortress walls from longboats, storming beach defenses, and conducting amphibious raids along hostile coastlines. Drawn from the youngest and fittest of the order's postulants, these marines combine the fanatical courage of crusading knights with the practical seamanship of Mediterranean sailors. They are the Order's fist, striking where the enemy least expects.

options.text: From sea to shore, the Cross advances.

advances.name: Colonial Administration
advances.text: The transition from a frontier military government to a mature colonial administration with civil courts, tax collectors, and provincial governors.

advances.name: African Naval Supremacy
advances.text: The kingdom's fleet dominates the central Mediterranean, its warships patrolling from Sicily to the Libyan coast.

advances.name: Studium of Tunis
advances.text: The school of Arabic that the Dominicans kept at Tunis in the thirteenth century is refounded as a studium for the whole kingdom. The settlers' sons learn their letters there, and the friars read and translate the Arabic books of the country.

advances.name: Modern Fortifications
advances.text: The kingdom's engineers adopt the latest European military science, creating layered defensive works that can withstand sustained bombardment and massed assault.

advances.name: African Granary
advances.text: The agricultural hinterland of Tunisia, once the breadbasket of Rome, is restored to full productivity under systematic European farming methods.

advances.name: Enlightened Order
advances.text: The military orders embrace Enlightenment principles of rational governance, scientific inquiry, and institutional reform while maintaining their religious foundations.

advances.name: Mediterranean Union
advances.text: The kingdom's unique position as a bridge between Europe and Africa enables it to broker diplomatic agreements and foster cooperation across the Mediterranean.

destiny.name: Destiny of Crusader Africa
destiny.text: The crusader kingdom has been forged in blood and faith. Now its destiny beckons, whether through the sword or through the ledger, Crusader Africa shall leave its mark upon the world.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: A Kingdom Forged
event.text: Crusader Africa stands. Where the Vandals, Byzantines, and Normans all tried and failed, we have carved a lasting Christian kingdom from the shores of Ifriqiya. Our banners fly from the walls of Tunis, our bells ring from the minarets we have consecrated as churches, and the Pope himself has blessed our enterprise. This is no temporary beachhead; this is a state, with laws, lands, and a destiny of its own.

destiny.name: The Sicilian Bridgehead
destiny.text: Sicily and Malta command the narrows of the Mediterranean. With Syracuse and Malta held, and three ribats garrisoned by the brother knights behind them, no fleet sails between east and west without our leave.

conditions.text: Chose Sword of the Cross
Own Syracuse, or a subject owns it
Own Malta, or a subject owns it
A Knights' Ribat stands in at least 3 of our locations

event.title: The Fall of Sicily
event.text: The great island fortress of Sicily has fallen to our armies. Syracuse, where Archimedes defied Rome, now opens its gates to the Cross of Africa. Malta, that barren rock in the narrows, is ours as well, and with it, mastery of every sea lane between the eastern and western Mediterranean. Our galley captains report that no hostile fleet can pass the Sicilian narrows without our knowledge and consent. The central sea is ours.

destiny.name: Outremer Reborn
destiny.text: The crusader kingdom reaches beyond Africa. Cyprus, the last outpost of the old Lusignan dynasty, must fly our banner. With Famagusta and Nicosia taken and a chain of six ribats held by the orders, a new Outremer stretches from Africa toward the Levantine shore.

conditions.text: Own Famagusta, or a subject owns it
Own Nicosia, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 50
A Knights' Ribat stands in at least 6 of our locations

event.title: The New Outremer
event.text: Cyprus is ours. The island where Richard the Lionheart once planted his banner, where the Lusignan kings built their doomed kingdom, where the Venetians grew rich on sugar and wine, all of it now belongs to the African crusade. Our chain of fortresses stretches from Tripoli to Famagusta, an unbroken line of Christian steel across the Mediterranean. The question now is how to use this power. Some counsel that we press on immediately, maintaining the momentum of holy war. Others argue that we should dig in, fortify what we hold, and build the garrisons that will hold these islands for centuries.

options.text: Press the crusade forward without pause.

modifiers.name: Crusade Momentum
modifiers.text: The holy war gains unstoppable momentum, armies reinforce quickly, the faithful bear the costs of war gladly, and the realm holds steady under the strain of constant campaigning.

modifiers.name: Garrison Doctrine
modifiers.text: Every conquered territory is immediately fortified and garrisoned, with supply lines extended to maintain the new positions. The navy is neglected in favor of this land-focused approach.

destiny.name: Kingdom of Jerusalem
destiny.text: The ultimate prize of every crusade is the Holy City itself. With the Cross planted upon the walls of Jerusalem, Acre, Antioch and Tripoli of Syria, the seats of the old crusader states, the dream that began at Clermont is fulfilled.

event.title: The Cross Upon the Holy City
event.text: Jerusalem. The word alone is worth more than a thousand arguments. The city where Christ walked, where Solomon built his temple, where Godfrey of Bouillon wept tears of joy upon its walls, it is ours. The African crusade, which began as an improbable beachhead on the shores of Tunis, has achieved what no Christian power has managed since Saladin's conquest. Acre, Antioch, Jerusalem, the entire Outremer is reborn under the banner of Crusader Africa. Now the question becomes: what shall this achievement mean? A perpetual war to expand the Kingdom of Heaven on Earth? Or a lasting peace, a Pax Christiana where the sword is sheathed and the Cross rules through justice?

options.text: The crusade never ends. Deus vult!

modifiers.name: Kingdom of Heaven
modifiers.text: The crusader kingdom claims divine mandate to wage holy war wherever the infidel holds sway. Wars are cheaper to declare and causes for war easier to find, though the kingdom has little patience left for the unbeliever within its own walls.

options.text: Let us build a lasting peace in the Holy Land.

modifiers.name: Pax Christiana
modifiers.text: The crusader kingdom imposes a Christian peace across the Levant, backed by diplomatic leverage and an extensive intelligence network that keeps potential rivals off-balance.

destiny.name: Master of the Narrows
destiny.text: The ports of Tunis and Tripoli sit upon the Mediterranean's waist, where every trade route must pass. Bring silk into your markets, fill your treasury, and prove that commerce is mightier than the sword.

Gold at least 1000

event.title: The Silk Roads of the Sea
event.text: Silk from the East, carried by Genoese and Venetian merchantmen, now passes through our ports. The customs houses of Tunis and Tripoli are filled with bales of shimmering fabric destined for the markets of Christendom. Our position at the Mediterranean's waist gives us leverage over every trade route, and our treasury swells with the duties we collect.

options.text: Let the wealth of the world flow through our ports.

destiny.name: The African Bourse
destiny.text: Italian banking houses have established branches in our ports, and the wealth of three continents flows through our customs. Build up Tunis, where the merchant nations keep their fondachi, and raise a dogana or a merchants quarter there through which every foreign cargo must pass, making it the Mediterranean's financial center.

conditions.text: Gold at least 2000
We own Tunis and its development is at least 47
We own Tunis and a Dogana, Merchants Quarters, Grand Marketplace or Commerce Center stands there

event.title: The Lombard Connection
event.text: Italian banking houses (Florentine, Genoese, Sienese) have opened permanent offices in our ports, drawn by the volume of trade flowing through the African narrows. Their letters of credit and bills of exchange oil the wheels of our commerce, while their capital finances new warehouses, docks, and market halls. We stand at a crossroads in how to manage this wealth. We might embrace the Italian banking model fully, adopting their sophisticated financial instruments and sound monetary policy. Or we might leverage our naval position more aggressively, using our corsair fleet to protect, and tax, the Mediterranean sea lanes.

options.text: Embrace Italian banking and sound finance.

modifiers.name: Lombard Banking
modifiers.text: Italian financial expertise stabilizes the kingdom's economy, offering favorable loan terms and keeping inflation in check while binding subject territories through economic dependence.

options.text: Let our fleet make the sea lanes profitable.

modifiers.name: Corsair Commerce
modifiers.text: The kingdom's warships double as merchant escorts and customs enforcers, ensuring that the sea lanes remain profitable and that devastation from piracy is quickly repaired.

destiny.name: Emporium Mundi
destiny.text: The ancient dream of a universal emporium, where the goods of Africa, Asia, and Europe change hands in a single marketplace. Seize Alexandria, attract the incense trade, amass a great fortune, and raise Tripoli, where the caravans of the Sahara reach the sea, into a great port.

event.title: Emporium of the World
event.text: The ancient dream is realized. Alexandria's harbor, once the gateway to the riches of the East, now flies our flag. Incense from Arabia, spices from India, silk from China, all of it passes through our customs houses on its way to the hungry markets of Europe. Our ports are the busiest in the Mediterranean, our merchants the wealthiest, our banks the most trusted. The question now is how to use this position. We might declare our ports free, open to all nations, exempt from the petty tariffs and trade wars that cripple commerce elsewhere. Or we might leverage our monopoly position to finance colonial ventures beyond the Mediterranean, reaching toward the wealth of the Atlantic and the Indian Ocean.

options.text: Declare our ports open to all the world.

modifiers.name: Free Port of Africa
modifiers.text: The ports of Crusader Africa are declared open to all nations, attracting merchants from every corner of the Mediterranean with promises of low tariffs and diplomatic neutrality.

options.text: Finance colonial ventures beyond the sea.

modifiers.name: Colonial Enterprise
modifiers.text: The wealth of Mediterranean trade finances colonial ventures beyond the familiar sea, reducing the costs of distant outposts and extending the kingdom's commercial reach into new markets.

units.name: Sergeants of Ifriqiya
units.text: Armored sergeants-at-arms who form the backbone of the crusader garrison. Equipped with mail, shield, and sword, they are disciplined defenders of Christendom's African outpost.

units.name: African Turcopole
units.text: Light cavalry scouts recruited from local converts and settlers of mixed heritage. Fast, familiar with the terrain, and deadly with bow and javelin, they serve as the kingdom's eyes and ears.

units.name: Presidio Musketeer
units.text: Professional garrison infantry armed with matchlock muskets, trained to defend the presidio fortresses against assault and sally forth to break sieges.

units.name: Corsair Galley
units.text: A fast, heavily-armed galley built for raiding and coastal patrol. Faster than standard galleys and mounting extra bow chasers, these vessels are the terror of hostile shipping.

units.name: African Levy Spearman
units.text: Local recruits armed with spear and shield, drawn from the convert population and settler communities. They lack the equipment of European regulars but know the land and fight for their homes.

units.name: Order Marine
units.text: Elite amphibious infantry of the military orders, trained to fight from ship to shore. They storm beaches, scale fortress walls from boats, and conduct raids deep behind enemy lines.

units.name: Order Xebec
units.text: A fast, lateen-rigged warship combining galley and sailing vessel. Favored by Mediterranean navies for its speed and agility, it excels at patrol, pursuit, and coastal interdiction.

buildings.name: Knights' Ribat
buildings.text: A ribat held by brother knights: a square of walls with a watchtower, a chapel where the prayer hall stood, and cells for the garrison around the court. Men are mustered and drilled within, and the country around looks to it in a siege.

buildings.name: Dogana
buildings.text: The crown's customs house in a port town. Cargoes are weighed and taxed in its court, sold at auction through its sworn interpreters, and the price is guaranteed by its officers. The foreign merchants keep their own fondachi; the dogana is where they must deal.

buildings.name: Coral Fishery
buildings.text: A station of coral boats on a coast where the red coral grows. A weighted wooden cross hung with nets is dragged over the banks, and the branches it tears loose are sorted and sold to the bead makers of Italy. Where the coral grows, more of it is brought up.

where.text: The location's raw material is Gems

buildings.name: Olive Press
buildings.text: A stone mill and press among the groves. The oil is drawn off into jars and carried down to the ports, and the groves around it yield more.

where.text: The location's raw material is Olives

buildings.name: Crusader Cathedral
buildings.text: A great church built in the Romanesque or Gothic style, seat of a bishop and center of the Catholic mission in Africa. Its schools teach Latin, its scriptorium copies manuscripts, and its bells call the faithful to prayer.

buildings.name: Presidio Fortress
buildings.text: A star-shaped coastal fortress garrisoned by professional soldiers, commanding a harbor or strategic approach. Its angled bastions and interlocking fields of fire make it nearly impregnable to conventional assault.

buildings.name: Pilgrim Hospice
buildings.text: A rest house maintained by the religious orders for pilgrims, travelers, and the sick. It provides food, shelter, and basic medical care along the roads of Crusader Africa.

buildings.name: Grain Warehouse
buildings.text: A fortified storehouse for the kingdom's wheat harvest, facilitating bulk export across the Mediterranean. The grain trade made Roman Africa wealthy, and the crusaders revive it.

buildings.name: African Academy
buildings.text: An institution of learning founded by the reformed military orders, combining European scholarship with practical instruction in navigation, engineering, and natural philosophy.

buildings.name: Holy Land Command
buildings.text: The supreme military headquarters of the crusading orders in the reconquered Holy Land, coordinating garrison defense, levy recruitment, and the fortification of conquered territory across the entire Outremer.

buildings.name: Mediterranean Exchange
buildings.text: A grand commercial exchange where merchants from across the Mediterranean conduct business, exchange currencies, and negotiate contracts. Its marble halls and counting rooms are the beating heart of African commerce.
